title: Operator grammar
goal: Think in verb + motion: d, c and y combine with every motion you know, and . repeats the last change.

lessons.title: Delete with d + motion

concepts.desc: delete over any motion: dw, de, db, d$, d0, dG, dgg, d}.
delete the whole line (operator doubled = act on the line).
delete to the end of the line (same as d$).
dw also eats the space after the word; de stops at the end of the word.
delete to the end / start of the file, linewise.

lessons.tip: Say it out loud: 'delete to end of word' = de. Every motion from week 1 is now a delete command.

quiz.q: Delete from the cursor to the end of the line?
What's the difference between dw and de?
quiz.a: dw deletes to the start of the next word (including trailing space); de deletes to the end of the current word.

quiz.q: Delete from the current line to the end of the file?
What does d} do?
quiz.a: Deletes from the cursor to the next blank line (end of the paragraph).

quiz.q: Delete the word before the cursor?
What does dd do?

lessons.title: Change with c + motion

concepts.desc: delete over a motion and enter insert mode: cw, c$, cb, c0.
special case: behaves like ce (doesn't eat the trailing space).
change the whole line (keeps indentation with autoindent).
change to the end of the line (same as c$).
substitute one character: delete it and enter insert mode.

lessons.tip: c is 'd, then i' in one go, and it's a single undoable, repeatable change. Prefer cw over dwi.

quiz.q: Replace the current word from the cursor onward?
Replace the rest of the line?
What does cc do?
quiz.a: Deletes the line's text and enters insert mode on it.

quiz.q: Difference between s and r?
quiz.a: s deletes the character and enters insert mode; r replaces it with one character and stays in normal mode.

quiz.q: Why is cw not the same as dwi?
quiz.a: cw acts like ce and keeps the space after the word; it's also a single repeatable change.

quiz.q: What does S do?
quiz.a: Same as cc: change the whole line.

lessons.title: Yank and put

concepts.desc: yank (copy) over a motion / the whole line.
put after / before the cursor (below / above for whole lines).
swap two characters.
move a line down / up (swap with the next line).
duplicate a line.
yank to the end of the line in Neovim (y$).

lessons.tip: Deleting also yanks: d and x are 'cut'. That's why xp and ddp work.

quiz.q: Duplicate the current line?
Swap the current line with the one below?
Fix 'teh' with the cursor on 'e'?
Difference between p and P for a yanked line?
quiz.a: p puts it below the current line, P above.

quiz.q: Copy the word under the cursor from its start?
quiz.a: yw (or yiw from anywhere in it)

quiz.q: Does dd put the line in a register?
quiz.a: Yes, deletes are yanked into the unnamed register, so p puts it back.

lessons.title: Counts and the dot command

concepts.desc: d3w, 3dd, 2yy, c2w: counts multiply motions.
d3w and 3dw do the same thing.
repeat the last change (including the text typed in an insert).
repeat the last change count times.
the classic pattern: make one change, then move and dot.

lessons.tip: Design changes to be repeatable: one change, then . everywhere else. If you're retyping something, you probably wanted the dot.

quiz.q: Delete the next three lines including this one?
What does . repeat?
quiz.a: The last change: the operator + motion, or the whole insert including the typed text.

quiz.q: Delete three words?
You appended ; to one line with A;<Esc>. How do you do the next line?
Yank two lines?
Does moving the cursor count as a change for .?
quiz.a: No, motions aren't repeated by .; only changes are.

lessons.title: Week 2 review

concepts.desc: operators (verbs)
motions (nouns)

concepts.keys: dd cc yy D C Y
concepts.desc: line shortcuts
putting and swapping
repetition

lessons.tip: Before typing, ask: which operator, which motion, and can I dot it?

quiz.q: Change the whole line?
Delete to the end of the line?
Move the current line up one?
quiz.a: ddkP (delete it, move up, put above)

quiz.q: Delete 2 lines, then repeat it 3 times?
Change the next two words?
Yank to the end of the file?
